title: BAW (Bulk Acoustic Wave) - Band 71 (600 MHz) for WiFi 6E Coexistence Filter
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Raj Patel

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a BAW (Bulk Acoustic Wave) filter targeting Band 71 (600 MHz) for WiFi 6E Coexistence Filter. The filter is designed on 128° YX LiNbO3 substrate with a target center frequency of 3161.5 MHz and bandwidth of 80.4 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the WiFi 6E Coexistence Filter module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: BAW (Bulk Acoustic Wave)
- Frequency Band: Band 71 (600 MHz)
- Application: WiFi 6E Coexistence Filter
- Substrate: 128° YX LiNbO3
- Package: Flip-Chip BGA
- Design Tool: Matlab RF Toolbox R2024b
- Design Center: San Jose Advanced Design Lab

This specification applies to all variants of the BAW (Bulk Acoustic Wave) design targeting Band 71 (600 MHz). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       3161.5 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       80.4 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 3.6 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 21.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 45.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 18.0 dB
Q Factor:               6533
Temperature Coefficient:-21.4 ppm/°C
Die Size:               2.1 x 2.0 mm
Wafer Size:             6-inch
Number of Resonators:   6
Electrode Material:     Mo
Passivation:            SiO2
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open Matlab RF Toolbox R2024b and load the BAW (Bulk Acoustic Wave) template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: 128° YX LiNbO3 with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 3161.5 MHz, BW 80.4 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 3.6 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (Flip-Chip BGA).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (6-inch, 128° YX LiNbO3).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Keysight N5227B PNA.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 9484 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 3.6 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 21.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 121 MHz offset >= 45.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 6 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 8.5 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +33 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 2000 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 85%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2024-09-04
Devices Tested:         65
Insertion Loss (meas):  3.28 dB
Return Loss (meas):     23.0 dB
Rejection (meas):       47.9 dB
Isolation (meas):       23.4 dB
Q Factor (meas):        6533
Group Delay Variation:  6.1 ns
Power Handling:         +31 dBm
Die Yield:              85.6%

Result Classification:  NEEDS REVIEW
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The BAW (Bulk Acoustic Wave) design demonstrated below-target performance for Band 71 (600 MHz).
b) Insertion loss is marginally above target; electrode thickness optimization recommended.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Temperature stability was within specification across full range.
e) Cross-talk between adjacent filter channels was below -55 dB.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Review near-band rejection margin for worst-case temperature.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Schedule follow-up measurement after design tweak.
